'''Landry Michael Shamet''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|æ|m|ɪ|t}})<ref>[https://www.nba.com/news/new-york-knicks-2025-26-pronunciation-guide New York Knicks 2025-26 Pronunciation Guide]. ''[[NBA.com]]''. Retrieved February 11, 2026.</ref> (born March 13, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]] and was selected 26th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He has also played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Phoenix Suns]], and [[Washington Wizards]].

==Early life==
Landry Shamet was born on March 13, 1997, in [[Kansas City, Missouri]], to Melanie Shamet, a single mother.<ref>{{cite web |title=Landry Shamet - Men's Basketball |url=https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/landry-shamet/3306 |website=Wichita State Athletics |access-date=November 20, 2020}}</ref> Melanie Shamet attended [[Boise State University]] on a volleyball scholarship. Shamet's father, [[Ron Davis (basketball)|Ron Davis]], is a former professional basketball player. Shamet did not know about his father until he was a teenager; he met him for the first time in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rankin |first1=Duane |title=Phoenix Suns: Landry Shamet meets father, siblings; solely focused on family, basketball |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2022/09/27/landry-shamet-meets-father-siblings-solely-focused-family-basketball/10441089002/ |website=AZ Central |access-date=May 12, 2023 |date=September 27, 2022}}</ref> Shamet is biracial.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1275673/2019/10/30/how-landry-shamets-old-soul-and-his-off-the-charts-hoops-sense-put-him-in-the-drivers-seat-in-l-a/ |title=How Landry Shamet's old soul, and his off-the-charts hoops sense, put him in the driver's seat in L.A.|work=The New York Times|last=Buha |first=Jovan|date=October 30, 2019}}</ref>

Shamet's uncle Tyler was a positive influence in his life growing up, and his extended family also provided support in his development. Shamet began playing basketball at the age of two. When he was in middle school, his family went bankrupt after the mortgage increased and they lost their duplex.<ref name=latimes1>{{cite news |last1=Greif |first1=Andrew |title=Landry Shamet's path to NBA began with strong family ties |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2019-10-24/landry-shamet-path-to-nba-began-with-strong-inner-circle |access-date=December 26, 2019 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=October 24, 2019}}</ref>

Shamet briefly attended [[Desborough College]] before attending [[Park Hill High School]] in Kansas City, where he was coached by David Garrison.<ref name=latimes1/>

==College career==
[[File:Landry Shamet.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Shamet with [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] in 2018]]
Shamet played three games in his freshman season before having to redshirt the season due to a foot injury. In January 2017, he became the point guard for the Shockers.<ref name="Suellentrop">{{cite news|last1=Paul|first1=Suellentrop|title=Wichita State's Landry Shamet taking first steps on national stage|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article139419493.html|access-date=December 7, 2017|work=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|date=March 18, 2017}}</ref> In his redshirt freshman season, Shamet averaged 11.4 points and 3.3 assists per game. He was named to the First team [[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] All-Conference and MVC Freshman of the Year. Following the season Shamet had surgery to repair a stress fracture on his foot.<ref name="rittenberg">{{cite news|last1=Rittenberg|first1=Adam|title=Landry Shamet scheduled for right foot surgery, out 12-16 weeks|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/20209587/landry-shamet-wichita-state-shockers-scheduled-right-foot-surgery-12-16-weeks|access-date=December 7, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|date=July 31, 2017}}</ref>

Coming into his sophomore year, Shamet was named to the Preseason First Team All-AAC and was one of fifty players named in the Preseason Wooden Award watch list.<ref name="Preseason media">{{cite press release|url=http://www.theamerican.org/news/2017/10/13/MBB_1013171801.aspx?path=mbball|title=Cincinnati Selected as 2017–18 American Men's Basketball Preseason Favorite|publisher=American Athletic |date=October 16, 2017|access-date=October 16, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Shamet named to Naismith Watch List|url=http://www.kwch.com/content/sports/Shamet-named-to-Naismith-Watch-List-456464793.html|access-date=December 7, 2017|work=KWCH12|date=November 9, 2017}}</ref> He was one of only two sophomores to be selected for the 2018 Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 list.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2018-01-11/college-basketball-john-r-wooden-award-midseason-top-25|title=College basketball: John R. Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 announced|date=2018-01-11|work=NCAA.com|access-date=2018-02-20|language=en}}</ref> Shamet scored a career-high 30 points to help Wichita State beat Oklahoma State 78–66 on December 9, 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Shamet scores 30; No. 6 Wichita St. tops Oklahoma St. 78-66|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988001|access-date=December 9, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 9, 2017}}</ref> Shamet led the AAC in several categories, including assists per game, true shooting percentage, and offensive box plus/minus. He also helped lead the Shockers to the NCAA Tournament each season he played.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/landry-shamet-1.html|title=Landry Shamet College Stats {{!}} College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2018-02-20}}</ref> He averaged 14.9 points and 5.2 assists per game as a sophomore. Following the season he declared for the 2018 NBA draft.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/14/wichita-state-landry-shamet-raises-profile-nba-draft-prospect Wichita State's Landry Shamet steadily becomes solid NBA Draft prospect]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2018–2019)===
Shamet was taken with the 26th pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/sixers-select-wichita-state-guard-landry-shamet-26th-pick-nba-draft|title=Sixers select Wichita State guard Landry Shamet with 26th pick in NBA draft|publisher=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]|last=Haughton|first=Matt|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 22, 2018}}</ref> In the 2018 preseason, Shamet averaged 8.8 points per game, with an 18-point performance in a 120–114 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in China.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCaffery |first1=Jack |title=Landry Shamet used preseason to prove Sixers made a good bet |url=https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/landry-shamet-used-preseason-to-prove-sixers-made-a-good/article_39fa94c6-cfde-11e8-baef-23dfd76acdbe.html |access-date=October 16, 2018 |work=[[Delaware County Daily Times]] |date=October 14, 2018 |archive-date=October 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017082146/https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/landry-shamet-used-preseason-to-prove-sixers-made-a-good/article_39fa94c6-cfde-11e8-baef-23dfd76acdbe.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Shamet scored a career-high 29 points off the bench on January 8, 2019, in a home victory over the Washington Wizards, including a Sixers rookie record 8 three-pointers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.nba.com/game/0021800600/|title=WAS vs PHI, 8 Jan 2019|publisher=[[NBA]]|date=January 8, 2019|access-date=January 9, 2019|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206150734/https://stats.nba.com/game/0021800600/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2019–2020)===
On February 6, 2019, Shamet was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-aquire-chandler-muscala-shamet-and-two-first-round-draft-picks|title=L.A. Clippers Acquire Chandler, Muscala, Shamet And Two First Round Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}}</ref> In his first game with them, he scored 17 points, 13 of which were in the 4th quarter, in a comeback from 28 down against the [[Boston Celtics]]. On April 15, in Game 2 of the first round against the Golden State Warriors, he scored 12 points and the game winning 3-pointer in a 31-point comeback leading to a 135–131 Clippers victory.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Eldridge |first1=Taylor |title=Landry Shamet hits go-ahead three vs. Warriors, capping largest NBA playoff comeback |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article229309059.html |access-date=June 11, 2020 |work=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |date=April 16, 2019}}</ref>

In Game 7 of the second round in the 2020 NBA playoffs, Shamet turned his ankle in the first quarter and had to leave the game, playing only six minutes. The Clippers lost 104–89 to the [[Denver Nuggets]] and were eliminated.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marty |first1=Sean |title=Former WSU guard Landry Shamet eliminated in Western Conference Semifinals |url=https://thesunflower.com/52277/sports/former-wsu-guard-landry-shamet-eliminated-in-western-conference-semifinals/ |access-date=September 18, 2020 |work=The Sunflower |date=September 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2020–2021)===
On November 19, 2020, Shamet was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade that sent [[Luke Kennard (basketball)|Luke Kennard]] to the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Landry Shamet, Bruce Brown and the Draft Rights to Reggie nelson Perry in Three-team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/11/19/brooklyn-nets-acquire-landry-shamet-bruce-brown-and-draft-rights-reggie-perry-three-team-trade |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 20, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}}</ref> On January 14, 2021, Shamet switched his number from 13 to 20 since [[James Harden]] was traded to the Nets and wanted to wear the number 13.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/james-harden-trade-landry-shamet-once-again-has-to-give-up-his-number-for-incoming-superstar-teammate/|title = James Harden trade: Landry Shamet, once again, has to give up his number for incoming superstar teammate}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2021/01/nets-james-harden-number-13-landry-shamet|title = How much did James Harden pay Landry Shamet to wear No. 13 with the Nets?|date = January 14, 2021}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2021–2023)===
On August 6, 2021, Shamet was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Jevon Carter]] and the draft rights to [[Day'Ron Sharpe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-acquire-landry-shamet-brooklyn|title=SUNS ACQUIRE LANDRY SHAMET FROM BROOKLYN|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}}</ref> On October 18, he signed a four-year, $43 million rookie scale extension with the Suns.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns giving Landry Shamet four-year, $43M contract extension|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/10/18/suns-giving-landry-shamet-four-year-43m-contract-extension/|access-date=February 23, 2022|website=NBC Sports|date=October 18, 2021}}</ref> On December 20, 2022, Shamet scored a career-high 31 points, including tying a franchise-record with 9 three-pointers made in a single game, in a 113–110 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ep-b24y7U2Y Landry Shamet ties Phoenix Suns franchise record with 9 three pointers.]</ref> . The record was shared with teammate [[Cameron Johnson]], and former Suns players [[Aron Baynes]], [[Channing Frye]], and [[Quentin Richardson]]. He later tied his career-high in points scored five days later on [[Christmas Day]] in an overtime loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. On May 7, 2023, Shamet scored 19 points during a 129–124 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]] during the [[2023 NBA playoffs|Western Conference Semifinals]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4497962/2023/05/08/suns-nuggets-game-4-landry-shamet/ Forget about star power: Suns’ Landry Shamet takes over in Game 4 win]</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2023–2024)===
On June 24, 2023, the Suns traded Shamet, along with [[Chris Paul]], four first-round pick swaps, and six second-round picks, to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Bradley Beal]], [[Jordan Goodwin]], and [[Isaiah Todd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Agree to Trade Beal to Phoenix, Acquire Paul, Shamet and Draft Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-agree-to-trade-beal-to-phoenix-acquire-paul-shamet-and-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref>

On July 6, 2024, Shamet was waived by the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Request Waivers on Shamet|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-request-waivers-on-shamet|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> 

===Westchester/New York Knicks (2024–present)===
On September 14, 2024, Shamet signed with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Landry Shamet to an Exhibit 9 Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-landry-shamet-to-an-exhibit-9-contract|website=NBA.com|date=September 14, 2024|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 19 amid suffering a dislocated shoulder in an NBA preseason game against the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on October 15.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Chuma Okeke, Landry Shamet and T.J. Warren.|number=1847742422064734246|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref>

On October 26, 2024, Shamet joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] after being selected in the 2024 NBA G League draft<ref>{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Select Matt Ryan (1st) and Landry Shamet (2nd) in the 2024-25 NBA G League Draft|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-select-matt-ryan-1st-and-landry-shamet-2nd-in-the-2024-25-nba-g-league-draft|website=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}}</ref> and on December 23, he re-signed with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|author=nykcmulqueen|title=New York Knicks Sign Landry Shamet|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-landry-shamet|website=NBA.com|date=December 23, 2024|access-date=December 23, 2024}}</ref> Shamet made 50 appearances for New York during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 5.7 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.

On September 11, 2025, Shamet re-signed with the Knicks on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web | last=Bondy | first=Stefan | title=Knicks re-sign Landry Shamet and another guard to round out roster after Ben Simmons flirtation | website=New York Post | date=2025-09-11 | url=https://nypost.com/2025/09/11/sports/knicks-re-sign-landry-shamet-after-ben-simmons-flirtation/ | access-date=2025-12-09}}</ref> On November 14, Shamet scored a career-high 36 points, helping the Knicks defeat the [[2025–26 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] 140–132.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Landry Shamet goes off for 36 to help Knicks beat Heat|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/landry-shamet-goes-off-36-030558354.html|access-date=November 30, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> On November 26, Shamet was ruled out for at least four weeks after suffering a sprained right shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Source: Knicks' Landry Shamet (shoulder) out at least 4 weeks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47110660/sources-knicks-landry-shamet-shoulder-least-4-weeks|access-date=December 22, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> In Game 1 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(3) New York Knicks vs. (4) Cleveland Cavaliers|Eastern Conference Finals]], Shamet played key defense and hit three crucial three pointers in the 4th quarter and overtime of the Knicks' 22-point comeback win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in overtime, 115–104. He made 11 of 12 three point attempts in this series for a 91.7% three point shooting percentage, the highest ever in an NBA postseason series for player attempting at least ten three point shots. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7293522/2026/05/19/knicks-cavaliers-comeback-playoffs-nba/|title=How did the Knicks beat the Cavs? Behind New York’s 30-8 run in Game 1 comeback|website=Athletic|last=Henderson|first=David|date=May 20, 2026|access-date=May 20, 2026}}</ref> In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Shamet helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the Spurs, 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref>

On June 29, 2026, Shamet re-signed with the Knicks on a four-year, $24 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=June 29, 2026 |title=Sources: Landry Shamet intends to ink 4-year deal with Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49219180/sources-landry-shamet-intends-ink-4-year-deal-knicks |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=espn.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NEW YORK KNICKS RE-SIGN LANDRY SHAMET|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-re-sign-landry-shamet|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2026|access-date=July 13, 2026}}</ref>
